Task: map the INTEGRATION and VENDOR BOUNDARIES for a frontend development lead's playbook.

Read /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/index.md IN FULL first (it likely has the ownership/status table), then read each of these enough to answer the questions below (read the header/overview/ownership/status sections in full; skim implementation detail):
01-sfcc.md, 02-contentful.md, 03-mulesoft.md, 04-omneo.md, 05-givex.md, 06-booxi.md, 07-adyen.md, 08-global-e.md, 09-google-maps.md, 10-recaptcha.md, 11-narvar.md, 12-didomi.md, 13-gtm.md, 14-inside-chat.md, 15-optimizely.md, 16-crazyegg.md, 17-measmerize.md, 18-vimeo.md

Also list and one-line-summarise everything in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/vendor/ (didomi.md, giveX.md, global-e.md, measmerize.md, mulesoft.md, optimizely.md, sparroSchema.md) and explain how .docs/vendor/ differs in purpose from .docs/integration/.

Then corroborate DOC vs CODE: for each integration, grep the actual codebase (overrides/, config/, package.json dependencies, .env.sample) for evidence it is actually wired up. E.g. `grep -ril "didomi\|adyen\|contentful\|omneo\|givex\|booxi\|narvar\|optimizely\|crazyegg\|measmerize\|global-e\|globale\|recaptcha\|gtm\|vimeo\|inside" overrides/ config/ .env.sample package.json`. This is how you distinguish LIVE from PLANNED — a doc existing does not mean the integration is built.

REPORT, as structured markdown:
1. A table: file | system | what it does in one line | owner/responsible party named in the doc | status (live in code / partially wired / doc-only-planned) | evidence for that status (file path or grep hit, or "no code references found").
2. Which integrations are consent-gated behind Didomi and what the fail-closed rule is.
3. Which integrations touch checkout/payment and therefore carry the "never silently substitute a different checkout/payment flow" rule.
4. Which integrations are owned by an external party (MuleSoft/SI partner/vendor) vs the frontend squads — i.e. where the frontend boundary actually is.
5. Any doc that looks STALE or contradicts the code (e.g. names a vendor that isn't in package.json, or a config key not in .env.sample).
6. **"What bites you"**: 5-10 specific non-obvious traps a lead would hit around these integrations.

Cite file:line for every claim. Be explicit about what you could not determine.

# PWA Integration Design Documents

These documents describe each external system that the Zimmermann PWA storefront interacts with **from the PWA layer** — either browser-direct or proxied through the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer. Each system has its own document covering purpose, scope, browser-side architecture, authentication, data exchange, consent gating, performance, multi-region behaviour, graceful degradation, security and privacy, and the open items requiring client input before implementation.

> **Scope.** PWA-layer only (browser-direct and MRT-proxied). Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here.

The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.

### Commerce backbone

The data sources every storefront page depends on.

| #   | System                                | Purpose                                                                | Document                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 1   | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders.               | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md)             |
| 2   | **Contentful**                        | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |

### Account and customer data

Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.

| #   | System                          | Purpose                                                                                        | Document                         |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 3   | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy.                  | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
| 4   | **Omneo**                       | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account.                                                | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md)       |
| 5   | **GiveX (balance check)**       | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX.                                 | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md)       |
| 6   | **Booxi**                       | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md)       |

### Checkout cluster

The buying flow.

| #   | System                            | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 7   | **Adyen**                         | Browser-side payment Drop-in for SFCC-owned domestic checkout.                                   | [07-adyen.md](07-adyen.md)             |
| 8   | **Global-e**                      | International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US international).                             | [08-global-e.md](08-global-e.md)       |
| 9   | **Google Maps Platform (Places)** | Address autocomplete at checkout, MRT-proxied.                                                   | [09-google-maps.md](09-google-maps.md) |
| 10  | **Google reCAPTCHA**              | Bot protection on register / login forms — browser loads script, MRT verifies token server-side. | [10-recaptcha.md](10-recaptcha.md)     |
| 11  | **Narvar**                        | Estimated Delivery Date widget at checkout, domestic only.                                       | [11-narvar.md](11-narvar.md)           |

### Cross-cutting overlays

Consent, analytics, and customer service — applied across every page rather than tied to a specific journey.

| #   | System                 | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 12  | **Didomi**             | Consent Management Platform — gatekeeper for every browser-loaded third-party script.            | [12-didomi.md](12-didomi.md)           |
| 13  | **Google Tag Manager** | Data layer, Consent Mode v2, downstream tag orchestration via Tell No Lies.                      | [13-gtm.md](13-gtm.md)                 |
| 14  | **Inside Chat**        | Customer-service chat widget.                                                                    | [14-inside-chat.md](14-inside-chat.md) |
| 15  | **Optimizely Web**     | A/B testing and personalisation — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                           | [15-optimizely.md](15-optimizely.md)   |
| 16  | **Crazy Egg**          | Heatmaps and session recording — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                            | [16-crazyegg.md](16-crazyegg.md)       |
| 17  | **Measmerize**         | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP.                                                 | [17-measmerize.md](17-measmerize.md)   |
| 18  | **Vimeo**              | Product video (PDP gallery) and editorial video (homepage and content pages via Contentful CMS). | [18-vimeo.md](18-vimeo.md)             |

## Note on runtime load order

The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. At runtime, **Didomi loads first** (document 11) because every other browser-loaded third-party script — GTM, Inside Chat, the Narvar widget, the Google Maps proxy call, and the Adyen Drop-in — is gated by Didomi consent. Each integration document records its own consent posture; the Didomi document is the single contract that all the others honour.

## Cross-cutting principles

- **Fail closed on consent.** If Didomi cannot determine consent state, no third-party tracking or marketing script loads.
- **Fail independently.** One vendor outage must not break the storefront — each integration has a documented degradation path.
- **LCP budget is ≤ 2.0 s at p75 mobile.** Any browser-loaded third-party script defers behind consent or hydration and does not block first paint.
- **Multi-region.** Eight SFCC sites across six regions, eleven active locales. Every integration that varies by region documents the per-storefront configuration matrix.
- **No secrets in the browser bundle.** Public and publishable keys only — anything that grants write access lives server-side, either in MRT environment variables or in SFCC Business Manager.

## Document template

Each integration document follows the same structure for ease of review:

1. Purpose and scope
2. Vendor relationship
3. Browser-side architecture
4. Authentication and credentials
5. Data exchanged
6. Consent and gating
7. Performance and loading strategy
8. Multi-region behaviour
9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
10. Security and privacy
11. Open items requiring client confirmation

Sections may merge where the surface is narrow (for example, the GiveX document folds observability into the security and privacy section) or removed when not applicable.

     1	# ── Environment switching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     2	# This file is the documented template for every variable the project uses. Each
     3	# active line below is preceded by its own `# scope:shared`, `# scope:tier`,
     4	# `# scope:personal`, or `# scope:auto` comment line (parsed by
     5	# scripts/switchEnv.mjs, ignored by everything else — kept on its own line,
     6	# not trailing on the KEY=value line, so a blank placeholder here still reads
     7	# as genuinely empty to the pre-commit secret guard):
     8	#   scope:shared   — same value across all 6 tiers (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod)
     9	#                    AND same for the whole team. Lives in .env.shared; included
    10	#                    in `push`/`init`'s pull to/from GitHub Environments.
    11	#   scope:tier     — differs per tier. Lives in the gitignored .env.<tier> for
    12	#                    whichever tier you're pointing local dev at; also
    13	#                    included in `push`/pull.
    14	#   scope:personal — tier-independent like shared, but a PERSONAL credential
    15	#                    (your own Atlassian token, your own Contentful CMA token)
    16	#                    that must never be centralized — still lives in
    17	#                    .env.shared, but `push`/`init`'s pull skip it entirely.
    18	#                    Each developer fills this in themselves.
    19	#   scope:auto     — never hand-set; scripts/switchEnv.mjs injects this itself.
    20	#
    21	# A second optional tag `# mrt:true` marks variables that belong in the MRT
    22	# Managed Runtime environment (storefront runtime config). Only keys tagged
    23	# `mrt:true` are synced by the "Sync Env Vars to MRT" GitHub Actions workflow.
    24	# CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
    25	# are NOT tagged — they are never synced to MRT.
    26	#
    27	# Commands (see scripts/switchEnv.mjs for details):
    28	#   npm run env -- init       — scaffold .env.shared + every .env.<tier> at once,
    29	#                                so you can fill in all tokens in one pass instead
    30	#                                of tier by tier
    31	#   npm run env -- validate   — check all existing env files: unknown/misplaced
    32	#                                keys, blanks, and cross-checks (e.g. a tier's
    33	#                                COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST actually matching that
    34	#                                tier's config/<tier>.js proxy host)
    35	#   npm run env -- validate --live — also makes a real read-only Contentful
    36	#                                Delivery API call AND a real SLAS guest
    37	#                                (client_credentials) token request per tier —
    38	#                                confirms credentials actually work, not just
    39	#                                that they're set. The SLAS check is the same
    40	#                                request every anonymous shopper visit already
    41	#                                triggers — no customer/commerce data touched.
    42	#   npm run env -- push <shared|dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod> — tier-1-approvers
    43	#                                only: upload a local file's values to the
    44	#                                matching GitHub Environment
    45	#   npm run env -- <tier>     — switch to <tier> (dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod)
    46	#
    47	# `init` also pulls values from GitHub Environments (one per scope — "shared"
    48	# plus one per tier — created under this repo's Settings > Environments) and
    49	# auto-fetches CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID / CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN /
    50	# CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN for every tier once .env.shared has a real
    51	# CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN + CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID — same read-only Content
    52	# Management API call and the same @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers write gate as
    53	# `npm run config:contentful`.
    54	#
    55	# NOTE — deliberate override (2026-07-13): GitHub Environment Variables are
    56	# plaintext and readable by any repo collaborator (no per-key ACL like
    57	# CODEOWNERS gives files) — they do not meet the bar AGENTS.md's "secrets only
    58	# in .env / Managed Runtime" rule sets. Using them here anyway was a conscious,
    59	# confirmed tradeoff for centralization; write access is restricted to repo
    60	# Admin (= tier-1-approvers), read access is repo-collaborator-wide by design.
    61	#
    62	# SFCC bootstrap values (org id / short code / OCAPI host / SLAS client id) are
    63	# never auto-fetched from SFCC itself — there's no discovery API, and SLAS
    64	# client secrets can't be read back after creation. Those still need a human to
    65	# enter them once (into .env.<tier> or via `push`), but from then on they're
    66	# centrally available via GitHub Environments like everything else here.
    67	
    68	# ── Commerce / SFCC ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    69	# Salesforce Commerce Cloud — BKZK-001 instance
    70	# scope:tier
    71	# mrt:true
    72	COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST=TODO
    73	# scope:tier
    74	# mrt:true
    75	COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID=TODO
    76	# scope:tier
    77	# mrt:true
    78	COMMERCE_API_SCAPI_HOST=
    79	# scope:shared
    80	# mrt:true
    81	COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE=qmyt7hks
    82	# scope:shared
    83	# mrt:true
    84	COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU
    85

    88	# mrt:true

    91	# mrt:true

    93	
    94	# scope:tier
    95	# mrt:true
    96	EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID=aaij-MobileFirst
    97	
    98	# ── PWA Kit base-template defaults ────────────────────────────────────────────
    99	# Referenced by config/default.js and overrides/app/ssr.js but may not be used by
   100	# this project. Marketing Cloud is the PWA Kit default for transactional emails
   101	# (password reset, passwordless login) — Zimmermann uses Emarsys via Omneo, so
   102	# these may be removed once the email/auth wiring is finalised.
   103	# scope:shared

   105	COMMERCE_AGENT_SETTINGS=

   124	
   125	# ── Google Maps API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   126	# Address autocomplete at checkout (delivery + billing) and PDP Find in Boutique
   127	# map/directions. Replaces Loqate/PCA Predict. (CFD-023/030/059, PRD-034)
   128	# scope:shared

   132	# ── Contentful (Preview + Delivery) ───────────────────────────────────────────
   133	# Single Contentful space across all tiers (confirmed 2026-07-11), but each

     1	/**
     2	 * Undici connection pools for SSR upstream origins (TSD §12.1 blast-radius mitigation).
     3	 *
     4	 * Each pool caps the concurrent connections to one origin so a slow or flooded integration
     5	 * cannot exhaust connections for unrelated services. Use the per-call `dispatcher` option
     6	 * on `fetch()` calls inside ssr.js to route requests through the correct pool:
     7	 *
     8	 *   import {fetch} from 'undici'
     9	 *   import {sfccPaymentsPool} from './ssr/connectionPools'
    10	 *   const data = await fetch(url, {dispatcher: sfccPaymentsPool})
    11	 *
    12	 * Connection caps and timeouts are set to the TSD §12.1 planned values.
    13	 * Validate them on Stage (§9.3) — undici emits queue-depth and connection-wait
    14	 * metrics via diagnostic channel events for tuning.
    15	 *
    16	 * IMPORTANT: Booxi base URL must be confirmed with the Integration team before enabling
    17	 * that pool. See the TODO below.
    18	 */

    25	);

=========== 01-sfcc.md (1-60, 82-100, 117-160) ===========
     1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
     2	
     3	## 1. Purpose and scope
     4	
     5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
     6	
     7	In scope:
     8	
     9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
    10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
    11	- Basket and cart
    12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
    13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
    14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
    15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
    16	
    17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
    18	
    19	Out of scope of this document:
    20	
    21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
    22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
    23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
    24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
    25	
    26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
    27	
    28	```
    29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
    30	        │
    31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
    32	        ▼
    33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
    34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
    35	        ▼
    36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
    37	        │
    38	        ▼
    39	SFCC realm
    40	```
    41	
    42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
    43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
    44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
    45	
    46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
    47	
    48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
    49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
    50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
    51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
    52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
    53	
    54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
    55	
    56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
    57	
    58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
    59	
    60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
    61	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
    62	
    63	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
    64	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
    65	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
    66	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
    67	
    68	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
    69	
    70	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
    71	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
    72	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
    73	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
    74	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
    75	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
    76	
    77	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
    78	
    79	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
    80	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
    81	
    82	| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
    83	| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    84	| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
    85	| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
    86	| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
    87	| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
    88	| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
    89	| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
    90	| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
    91	| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |
    92	
    93	## 9. Security and privacy
    94	
    95	- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
    96	- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
    97	- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
    98	- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.
    99	
   100	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
   101	
   102	1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.
   103	
   104	2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) holds `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl`'s origin in a pool separate from `sfcc-scapi` (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). That separation only provides blast-radius isolation if the two hosts are different origins. If `sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to the same SCAPI host, the pools should be merged.

=========== 02-contentful.md ===========
# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
- Live preview in Contentful Studio
- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
...[76-150]...
## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

=========== 03-mulesoft.md ===========
# 03 — MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads via MRT proxy)

## 1. Purpose and scope

MuleSoft is the integration middleware that sits between SFCC and Zimmermann's back-office systems (NewStore OMS, AP21, Omneo, Narvar). The vast majority of MuleSoft traffic is server-to-server from SFCC and is out of scope here. This document covers the **separate, direct path** in which the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer calls MuleSoft directly via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of read operations where SFCC adds no value to the round-trip.

Operations in scope of this document (PWA → MRT → MuleSoft, with SFCC outside the read path):

- Order history list (CRM-056 / CRM-057, RRC-013) — the 50 most recent orders, online and in-store
- Order detail (CRM-071 / CRM-072)
- Account dashboard "recent orders" summary (CRM-029, OM-017, OM-035)
- Returns data for the My Account returns view (CRM-088)
- Real-time stock availability:
  - Find in Boutique flyout and BOPIS boutique selection screen (CFD-043, CAI-038)
  - Collect in Boutique store + size validation (CAI-043)
  - Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034 — this MuleSoft flow does not yet exist; the storefront falls back to the inventory feed until it is built)
- GiveX balance check (GC-037, GC-053) — MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX TCP connection and credentials

=========== 04-omneo.md ===========
# 04 — Omneo (Communication Preferences iFrame)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Omneo is the system of record for customer identity and loyalty. Most Omneo traffic is server-to-server via SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo and is out of scope here. The only surface where the PWA storefront talks to Omneo directly is a single embedded iFrame inside My Account (CRM-174 – CRM-177). The iFrame is the confirmed PRD approach (CRM-174 — enhancement logged to move into SFCC). Per CRM-174, the iFrame currently contains:

- **Communication Preferences** — the customer views and updates marketing and service preferences (CRM-175, CRM-176).
- **Region/country selection** — allows the customer to select location, state, and language preference.
- **Three clickable images** that open the respective PLP within the iFrame itself; this PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is logged in the Enhancement Log and is not in scope at launch.

Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. Omneo's documented embed is, however, a Shopify theme extension; the gating question for this non-Shopify (PWA) build is the auth handshake, covered in §9 (Open items).

In scope:

- The Communication Preferences iFrame and its host page on My Account
- Issuance of the customer-scoped credential that authorises the iFrame
- Embedding, sizing, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser

Out of scope of this document (handled server-side, outside the PWA layer):

- Profile, address book, order history, loyalty reads and writes
- The DMU-004 "profile read from Omneo at login" round trip — load-bearing, but executed by SFCC; the PWA only consumes the resulting customer object via the Commerce SDK
- The Omneo → Emarsys email-marketing handoff

The Zimmermann CRM team owns the preference categories, labels, and translations rendered inside the widget. The storefront embeds the widget only — no preference business logic lives in the storefront.

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
My Account → "Communication Preferences" route
        │
        ▼
Server (SSR or MRT endpoint):
  • Reads the authenticated SFCC customer
  • Mints a customer-scoped credential for the embed. The exact handshake
    is unconfirmed (§9); the two candidate mechanisms are:
        (a) signed URL / HMAC — signature = HMAC-SHA256( customerId, omneo_secret )
        (b) a server-minted, short-lived, profile-scoped JWT (an Omneo
            IDToken), obtained by a trusted backend calling Omneo's auth
            endpoint with an admin token, then handed to the browser
  • Returns the iFrame URL (and, for (b), the IDToken) to the client
        │
        ▼
Browser renders the iFrame against the Omneo host, carrying whichever
customer-scoped credential the confirmed handshake requires
        │
        ▼
Omneo iFrame:
  • Validates the credential, opens a scoped session for that profile only
  • Reads and writes preferences directly against Omneo
  • On save, Omneo emits a webhook to SFCC via MuleSoft (CRM-177);
    SFCC reflects the new state on the next Commerce SDK customer read
```

- The iFrame is rendered only for authenticated customers on the Communication Preferences route. There is no guest path.
- The credential is minted on the server so that neither an HMAC secret nor an Omneo admin token ever reaches the browser bundle or enters the React component tree as a build-time value — regardless of which handshake is confirmed.
- Saves originate inside the iFrame and write directly to Omneo (CRM-176). The PWA does not POST preference data itself.
- The PWA does not attempt to read or scrape the iFrame DOM — it is cross-origin and a hard boundary. State reflection in SFCC is handled by the webhook flow.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- **Auth pattern (unconfirmed — see §9):** the embed is authorised by a customer-scoped credential minted server-side. The exact mechanism for a non-Shopify (PWA) embed is not confirmed; two candidates are carried:
  - **(a) Signed URL / HMAC** — `customerId` plus an HMAC-SHA256 signature of that ID using an Omneo-issued secret. This is the approach this document originally assumed.
  - **(b) Server-minted profile-scoped JWT (`IDToken`)** — a trusted backend calls Omneo's auth endpoint with an admin token to mint a short-lived, profile-scoped JWT, which is then handed to the browser for the embed. This is the mechanism Omneo's developer docs ("Using Omneo ID") actually document; note it is explicitly not an HMAC. (HMAC appears in Omneo's docs only for Shopify app-proxy request signing, a separate Shopify-only concern.)
- **Customer ID source:** the Omneo customer ID is stored on the SFCC customer record alongside the email at migration (DMU-004); under (a) it is the value signed by the HMAC, and under (b) it scopes the minted JWT. The SFCC customer ID and the customer email are not used as the credential input.
- **Secret / token location:** whichever credential the confirmed handshake requires (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is held in SFCC Business Manager alongside the rest of the SFCC ↔ Omneo credentials, and the minting is performed server-side (e.g. an SCAPI custom endpoint). This keeps all Omneo credentials in one place and reuses the existing rotation procedure. (Contingent on the embed mechanism confirmed in §9.)
- **No Omneo credential in the browser bundle.** The browser only ever receives the assembled URL and, under (b), a short-lived customer-scoped token — never the HMAC secret or the admin token.
- **Credential freshness:** the credential is regenerated on every visit to the Communication Preferences route — it is not cached in the SCAPI response body, not persisted, and not stored in `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`. A minted JWT is additionally short-lived by design.
- **ITP / ETP resilience:** anti-tracking browsers (Safari ITP, Firefox ETP) may block third-party cookies inside the iFrame. Because auth is carried in the URL (or, under (b), in a URL parameter), cookie blocking does not break the experience.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → SFCC | Authenticated customer's SLAS access token | Standard Commerce SDK request |
...[97-130]...
## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Credential-mint round trip fails (SFCC unreachable or signing endpoint errors) | Render an explicit retry UI on the Communication Preferences page. Do not render the iFrame with a stale or unsigned URL. Per the TSD graceful-degradation contract for Omneo: never render partial data. |
| URL is assembled but the iFrame fails to load (CSP violation, Omneo CDN outage, network block) | Show a retry CTA inside the iFrame slot. After two consecutive failures, surface a contact-support message and a link to the storefront's privacy/contact page so the customer can manage preferences via support. (Design decision — exact fallback UX not specified in CRM-174–177; confirm with UX/product.) |
| iFrame loads but an Omneo-internal save fails | Owned by the widget's own UX — the PWA does not intercept. |
| Customer is unauthenticated when navigating to the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No credential-mint request is issued. |
| Omneo rotates or revokes the customer-auth credential (HMAC secret or Omneo admin token, depending on the confirmed handshake) | Rotation is handled in SFCC BM by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |

## 8. Security and privacy

- A single customer-scoped credential, minted server-side, is the entire auth surface presented to Omneo. Which credential that is depends on the handshake confirmed in §9 — either an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the customer ID, or a server-minted short-lived profile-scoped JWT (`IDToken`). The underlying secret (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is stored in SFCC BM, never in the PWA bundle, never logged, and rotated per the standard SFCC credential rotation policy.
- The `<iframe>` element uses the minimum `sandbox` flags required for the widget to function — at minimum `allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`, and `allow-same-origin`. The exact final set is confirmed during integration testing against the live Omneo widget.
- `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` is set on the `<iframe>` so the customer's storefront URL does not appear in Omneo's referer logs.
- Omneo's host is added to the storefront `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` directives. No wildcard Omneo subdomain is allowed.
- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), the customer record is removed from SFCC and Omneo through the SFCC GDPR cartridge and the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo chain. The Communication Preferences widget itself has no separate erasure flow.

## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

# 04 — Omneo (Communication Preferences iFrame)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Omneo is the system of record for customer identity and loyalty. Most Omneo traffic is server-to-server via SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo and is out of scope here. The only surface where the PWA storefront talks to Omneo directly is a single embedded iFrame inside My Account (CRM-174 – CRM-177). The iFrame is the confirmed PRD approach (CRM-174 — enhancement logged to move into SFCC). Per CRM-174, the iFrame currently contains:

- **Communication Preferences** — the customer views and updates marketing and service preferences (CRM-175, CRM-176).
- **Region/country selection** — allows the customer to select location, state, and language preference.
- **Three clickable images** that open the respective PLP within the iFrame itself; this PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is logged in the Enhancement Log and is not in scope at launch.

Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. Omneo's documented embed is, however, a Shopify theme extension; the gating question for this non-Shopify (PWA) build is the auth handshake, covered in §9 (Open items).

In scope:

- The Communication Preferences iFrame and its host page on My Account
- Issuance of the customer-scoped credential that authorises the iFrame
- Embedding, sizing, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser

Out of scope of this document (handled server-side, outside the PWA layer):

- Profile, address book, order history, loyalty reads and writes
- The DMU-004 "profile read from Omneo at login" round trip — load-bearing, but executed by SFCC; the PWA only consumes the resulting customer object via the Commerce SDK
- The Omneo → Emarsys email-marketing handoff

The Zimmermann CRM team owns the preference categories, labels, and translations rendered inside the widget. The storefront embeds the widget only — no preference business logic lives in the storefront.

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
My Account → "Communication Preferences" route
        │
        ▼
Server (SSR or MRT endpoint):
  • Reads the authenticated SFCC customer
  • Mints a customer-scoped credential for the embed. The exact handshake
    is unconfirmed (§9); the two candidate mechanisms are:
        (a) signed URL / HMAC — signature = HMAC-SHA256( customerId, omneo_secret )
        (b) a server-minted, short-lived, profile-scoped JWT (an Omneo
            IDToken), obtained by a trusted backend calling Omneo's auth
            endpoint with an admin token, then handed to the browser
  • Returns the iFrame URL (and, for (b), the IDToken) to the client
        │
        ▼
Browser renders the iFrame against the Omneo host, carrying whichever
customer-scoped credential the confirmed handshake requires
        │
        ▼
Omneo iFrame:
  • Validates the credential, opens a scoped session for that profile only
  • Reads and writes preferences directly against Omneo
  • On save, Omneo emits a webhook to SFCC via MuleSoft (CRM-177);
    SFCC reflects the new state on the next Commerce SDK customer read
```

- The iFrame is rendered only for authenticated customers on the Communication Preferences route. There is no guest path.
- The credential is minted on the server so that neither an HMAC secret nor an Omneo admin token ever reaches the browser bundle or enters the React component tree as a build-time value — regardless of which handshake is confirmed.
- Saves originate inside the iFrame and write directly to Omneo (CRM-176). The PWA does not POST preference data itself.
- The PWA does not attempt to read or scrape the iFrame DOM — it is cross-origin and a hard boundary. State reflection in SFCC is handled by the webhook flow.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- **Auth pattern (unconfirmed — see §9):** the embed is authorised by a customer-scoped credential minted server-side. The exact mechanism for a non-Shopify (PWA) embed is not confirmed; two candidates are carried:
  - **(a) Signed URL / HMAC** — `customerId` plus an HMAC-SHA256 signature of that ID using an Omneo-issued secret. This is the approach this document originally assumed.
  - **(b) Server-minted profile-scoped JWT (`IDToken`)** — a trusted backend calls Omneo's auth endpoint with an admin token to mint a short-lived, profile-scoped JWT, which is then handed to the browser for the embed. This is the mechanism Omneo's developer docs ("Using Omneo ID") actually document; note it is explicitly not an HMAC. (HMAC appears in Omneo's docs only for Shopify app-proxy request signing, a separate Shopify-only concern.)
- **Customer ID source:** the Omneo customer ID is stored on the SFCC customer record alongside the email at migration (DMU-004); under (a) it is the value signed by the HMAC, and under (b) it scopes the minted JWT. The SFCC customer ID and the customer email are not used as the credential input.
- **Secret / token location:** whichever credential the confirmed handshake requires (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is held in SFCC Business Manager alongside the rest of the SFCC ↔ Omneo credentials, and the minting is performed server-side (e.g. an SCAPI custom endpoint). This keeps all Omneo credentials in one place and reuses the existing rotation procedure. (Contingent on the embed mechanism confirmed in §9.)
- **No Omneo credential in the browser bundle.** The browser only ever receives the assembled URL and, under (b), a short-lived customer-scoped token — never the HMAC secret or the admin token.
- **Credential freshness:** the credential is regenerated on every visit to the Communication Preferences route — it is not cached in the SCAPI response body, not persisted, and not stored in `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`. A minted JWT is additionally short-lived by design.
- **ITP / ETP resilience:** anti-tracking browsers (Safari ITP, Firefox ETP) may block third-party cookies inside the iFrame. Because auth is carried in the URL (or, under (b), in a URL parameter), cookie blocking does not break the experience.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → SFCC | Authenticated customer's SLAS access token | Standard Commerce SDK request |
...[97-130]...
## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Credential-mint round trip fails (SFCC unreachable or signing endpoint errors) | Render an explicit retry UI on the Communication Preferences page. Do not render the iFrame with a stale or unsigned URL. Per the TSD graceful-degradation contract for Omneo: never render partial data. |
| URL is assembled but the iFrame fails to load (CSP violation, Omneo CDN outage, network block) | Show a retry CTA inside the iFrame slot. After two consecutive failures, surface a contact-support message and a link to the storefront's privacy/contact page so the customer can manage preferences via support. (Design decision — exact fallback UX not specified in CRM-174–177; confirm with UX/product.) |
| iFrame loads but an Omneo-internal save fails | Owned by the widget's own UX — the PWA does not intercept. |
| Customer is unauthenticated when navigating to the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No credential-mint request is issued. |
| Omneo rotates or revokes the customer-auth credential (HMAC secret or Omneo admin token, depending on the confirmed handshake) | Rotation is handled in SFCC BM by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |

## 8. Security and privacy

- A single customer-scoped credential, minted server-side, is the entire auth surface presented to Omneo. The underlying secret (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is stored in SFCC BM, never in the PWA bundle, never logged, and rotated per the standard SFCC credential rotation policy.

- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), the customer record is removed from SFCC and Omneo through the SFCC GDPR cartridge and the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo chain. The Communication Preferences widget itself has no separate erasure flow.

=========== 05-givex.md ===========
# 05 — GiveX (Gift Cards)

## 1. Purpose and scope

GiveX is Zimmermann's gift card and credit note processor. This document covers the PWA surfaces that directly call GiveX via MRT:

- The **balance-check input** in My Account (GC-051–062) and the "Check Balance" link in the checkout gift card entry field (GC-037). Both use the same MRT endpoint: `POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance`.
- The **gift card purchase experience** (§12) — the PWA renders the product, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists them on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side and is not a PWA-direct call.

Out of scope (server-side, not a PWA-direct path):

- Gift card and credit note validate / redeem / refund at checkout (GC-034–049) — handled via the NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX. The PWA sees only the resulting payment-instrument state from SCAPI.
- Gift card issuance at purchase — SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX.
- GiveX validate / redeem / refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44).
- Reversal on capture failure — handled server-side by NewStore / SFCC.

## 2. Vendor relationship

GiveX is reached via MuleSoft — the PWA never holds a GiveX credential or makes a direct GiveX call. For the balance check, MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket, host failover, and credentials internally; the PWA calls MuleSoft over HTTPS. Redemption at checkout goes via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft, outside the PWA boundary.

## 3. PWA-layer architecture

```
My Account (GC-051) / Checkout "Check Balance" link (GC-037)
        │
        ▼
Customer enters gift card or credit note number and PIN
        │
        ▼
Browser: POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance
   body: { number, pin }
        │
        ▼
MRT Node layer:
   1. Applies rate-limit and bot protection on this route
      (no per-customer cap — GC-062 — but route is hardened
       with WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA per
       GiveX security guidance)
   2. Forwards over HTTPS to MuleSoft with the MuleSoft API token
      held as an MRT environment variable
        │
        ▼
MuleSoft → GiveX (internal — MuleSoft's responsibility)
        │
        ▼
MuleSoft → MRT → Browser:
   { maskedNumber, balance, currency, expiry, error? }
        │
        ▼
PWA renders the result inline beside the input (GC-054, GC-055)
```

The browser never sees a GiveX credential or raw GiveX error. It sees only an HTTPS request to the storefront's own MRT origin and a typed JSON response.

Both the My Account balance check and the checkout Check Balance link (GC-037) use the same MRT endpoint. Login is not required for either (GC-059).

The balance check requires both the card number and its PIN, for both gift cards and credit notes. Zimmermann's GiveX merchant program has secure PINs enabled, so the PIN field is mandatory on every request. The PIN is a payment credential — see §9.

The customer can check another card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055). The same input field accepts both gift card and credit note numbers (GC-057).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| MuleSoft API token | MRT environment variable; injected on outbound request | Secret — never reaches the browser |

The customer is not required to be authenticated (GC-059). The call is not bound to a SLAS JWT.

## 5. Data exchanged

...[100,145]...
## 9. Security and privacy

- Card number and PIN are submitted in the POST body only — never as a URL query string. Query strings appear in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
- No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
- No `console.log`, Sentry breadcrumb, GTM dataLayer push, or analytics event may contain the card number or PIN. The logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must include a redaction rule for this route. No body-logging middleware on the balance-check route.
- After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). MuleSoft strips the prefix and check digit before the response reaches MRT.
- The MRT balance-check route applies WAF, bot management, rate-limit, and CAPTCHA, because the underlying MuleSoft credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper. There is no per-customer cap (GC-062); per-IP and per-session limits are enforced at the edge.

## 10. Gift card purchase (PWA surface)

The storefront sells gift cards as products. The PWA renders the PDP, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists gift metadata on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side after payment capture — the PWA makes no GiveX call on this path.

**Scope (confirmed):**
- Purchase — domestic storefronts only at launch; international purchase is a future roadmap item.
- Redemption (using a gift card as payment) — domestic storefronts only; not at Global-e international checkout at launch (GC-050).
- Balance check — all storefronts (GC-059).

**Two products:** Physical and digital gift cards are separate SFCC product IDs. Physical cards ship; digital cards send an email to the recipient.

**Fixed denominations:** $100, $200, $250, $300, $500. Selected via a searchable dropdown (GC-001–004). The PWA renders the selector from SCAPI product data — the set can change without a code change.

**Gift details captured at add-to-cart:** sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003). The PWA validates recipient email format, delivery date within 3 months, and personal-message length (GC-005–007).

**Data flow:** Gift metadata is attached to the basket line item as custom attributes via SCAPI. The PWA persists the metadata and does not call GiveX.

**PII:** Recipient name and email are third-party personal data. Carried over HTTPS, not logged beyond SFCC requirements, and subject to the standard data-handling posture.

## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** MuleSoft to publish the request and response schema for the balance-check endpoint (including the card number and PIN fields), the error taxonomy mapping GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, and the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the call cannot be implemented against a real MuleSoft instance.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request. If yes, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

# 06 — Booxi (PWA-direct appointment history via MRT proxy)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Booxi is the system of record for boutique appointment data (CRM-166 — the requirement sheet originally referenced "Booksy"; this was a typo, Booxi is the correct vendor). Customer appointment history surfaces within My Account, read directly from the Booxi API by the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`. This is a **PWA-direct path** — it does **not** transit SFCC or MuleSoft.

The requirement covers appointment history display only (CRM-165–167); storefront scope and timeline are still TBC. CRM-167 requires the My Account appointments section to be structured so it can be incorporated without structural redesign when Booxi is ready. This document describes the integration shape so the section can be slotted in later without rework; the precise contract is finalised once Booxi confirms its API (see §11).

In scope of this document:

- Appointment history list rendered inside My Account, read PWA → MRT → Booxi (CRM-165)
- The MRT proxy leg that holds the Booxi credential and identifies the customer to Booxi
- Embedding, loading, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser

Out of scope of this document:

- Appointment **creation, rescheduling, and cancellation** — not in the current PWA scope. Booking is handled in Booxi's own surfaces; the storefront reads history only. If in-storefront booking is later confirmed, it is added here as a separate write path.
- Any SFCC or MuleSoft involvement — there is none on this path.

## 2. Vendor relationship

- **Vendor:** Booxi — appointment scheduling platform; system of record for Zimmermann boutique appointment data (CRM-166).
- **PWA's relationship:** Booxi is consumed read-only. The API contract is owned by Booxi / the Zimmermann CRM team; the PWA team is not a co-developer of the API.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

The flow below is the recommended design. It is not yet a fixed contract — the customer-identification mechanism is pending confirmation with Booxi (see §11), and the specifics below would change if another scheme is agreed.

```
Browser (My Account → Appointments section)
        │  Customer's SLAS access token (JWT) is present after SFCC login
        ▼
PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/booxi/<endpoint>
   Authorization: Bearer <SLAS access token>
        │
        ▼
MRT Node layer:
   1. Validates the SLAS JWT signature against SFCC's published JWKS
   2. Drops the inbound Authorization header and sets the Booxi credential
      header instead (Booxi authenticates via its own `Booxi-PartnerKey`
      header, not a bearer `Authorization` header)
   3. Resolves the customer's Booxi identity (see §4) and scopes the request to it
   4. Forwards to https://<booxi-host>/<endpoint>
        │
        ▼
Booxi API:
   • Authorises the request via the Booxi API credential
   • Returns the customer's appointment history
        │
        ▼
Booxi response → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields the section needs)
```

- The browser never carries the Booxi credential. The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and is appended only on the MRT → Booxi leg.
- The appointments section is read-only and authenticated — it renders only for a logged-in customer on the My Account route.
- The section is built as a self-contained module so it can be enabled when Booxi is ready without restructuring the surrounding My Account page (CRM-167).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Booxi Partner API key (sent in the `Booxi-PartnerKey` header) | MRT environment variable; injected by MRT before forwarding | Secret — Booxi mandates this key is used server-side only and never reaches the browser |
| Customer SLAS access token (JWT) | Forwarded from the browser to MRT; used by MRT to authenticate the customer | Sensitive — proves user identity |
| SFCC JWKS | Used by MRT to verify the SLAS JWT signature | Public |

- **No Booxi credential in the browser bundle.** The Booxi credential is held server-side as an MRT environment variable, appended on the MRT → Booxi leg only.
- **Customer identification (open — see §11).** The PWA must prove *which* customer's appointments to return without letting the browser request an arbitrary customer's data. The recommended approach is that MRT validates the customer's SLAS JWT and resolves the corresponding Booxi customer reference server-side (from a Booxi customer ID held on the SFCC/Omneo profile, or via a Booxi lookup), then scopes the request to that reference. MRT must never accept a raw Booxi customer ID, email, or appointment ID from the browser as the identity input.
- One Booxi API credential per environment. Rotation cadence and named owner are tracked in §11.

## 5. Data exchanged
...[93,130]...
## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

For the balance check, MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket, host failover, and credentials internally; the PWA calls MuleSoft over HTTPS. Redemption at checkout goes via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft, outside the PWA boundary.

## 3. PWA-layer architecture

```
My Account (GC-051) / Checkout "Check Balance" link (GC-037)
        │
        ▼
Customer enters gift card or credit note number and PIN
        │
        ▼
Browser: POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance
   body: { number, pin }
        │
        ▼
MRT Node layer:
   1. Applies rate-limit and bot protection on this route
      (no per-customer cap — GC-062 — but route is hardened
       with WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA per
       GiveX security guidance)
   2. Forwards over HTTPS to MuleSoft with the MuleSoft API token
      held as an MRT environment variable
        │
        ▼
MuleSoft → GiveX (internal — MuleSoft's responsibility)
        │
        ▼
MuleSoft → MRT → Browser:
   { maskedNumber, balance, currency, expiry, error? }
        │
        ▼
PWA renders the result inline beside the input (GC-054, GC-055)
```

The browser never sees a GiveX credential or raw GiveX error. It sees only an HTTPS request to the storefront's own MRT origin and a typed JSON response.

Both the My Account balance check and the checkout Check Balance link (GC-037) use the same MRT endpoint. Login is not required for either (GC-059).

The balance check requires both the card number and its PIN, for both gift cards and credit notes. Zimmermann's GiveX merchant program has secure PINs enabled, so the PIN field is mandatory on every request. The PIN is a payment credential — see §9.

The customer can check another card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055). The same input field accepts both gift card and credit note numbers (GC-057).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| MuleSoft API token | MRT environment variable; injected on outbound request | Secret — never reaches the browser |

The customer is not required to be authenticated (GC-059). The call is not bound to a SLAS JWT.

## 5. Data exchanged

...[100,145]...
## 9. Security and privacy

- Card number and PIN are submitted in the POST body only — never as a URL query string. Query strings appear in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
- No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
- No `console.log`, Sentry breadcrumb, GTM dataLayer push, or analytics event may contain the card number or PIN. The logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must include a redaction rule for this route. No body-logging middleware on the balance-check route.
- After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). MuleSoft strips the prefix and check digit before the response reaches MRT.
- The MRT balance-check route applies WAF, bot management, rate-limit, and CAPTCHA, because the underlying MuleSoft credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper. There is no per-customer cap (GC-062); per-IP and per-session limits are enforced at the edge.

## 10. Gift card purchase (PWA surface)

The storefront sells gift cards as products. The PWA renders the PDP, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists gift metadata on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side after payment capture — the PWA makes no GiveX call on this path.

**Scope (confirmed):**
- Purchase — domestic storefronts only at launch; international purchase is a future roadmap item.
- Redemption (using a gift card as payment) — domestic storefronts only; not at Global-e international checkout at launch (GC-050).
- Balance check — all storefronts (GC-059).

**Two products:** Physical and digital gift cards are separate SFCC product IDs. Physical cards ship; digital cards send an email to the recipient.

**Fixed denominations:** $100, $200, $250, $300, $500. Selected via a searchable dropdown (GC-001–004). The PWA renders the selector from SCAPI product data — the set can change without a code change.

**Gift details captured at add-to-cart:** sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003). The PWA validates recipient email format, delivery date within 3 months, and personal-message length (GC-005–007).

**Data flow:** Gift metadata is attached to the basket line item as custom attributes via SCAPI. The PWA persists the metadata and does not call GiveX.

**PII:** Recipient name and email are third-party personal data. Carried over HTTPS, not logged beyond SFCC requirements, and subject to the standard data-handling posture.

## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** MuleSoft to publish the request and response schema for the balance-check endpoint (including the card number and PIN fields), the error taxonomy mapping GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, and the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the call cannot be implemented against a real MuleSoft instance.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request. If yes, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
